findings: The proposed scope report cannot show every changed record: it omits uncommitted `.factory/` changes, although the approved story plan requires the stage-base diff plus working tree with no exclusions (plans/active/FORGE-ACCESS-1-full-access-forge-judges-the-result-not-each-write.md:65; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/task-plans/CODE.md:135). It also puts records in a separate category without saying whether a record outside the declared scope appears in the promised outside-scope list (.factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/task-plans/CODE.md:137).

Overlap detection is narrower than the promised 'another active task': the plan checks only outside-scope paths using `active_stages_everywhere`, which returns active stages of the current story only. An in-scope path that overlaps another task, or a path overlapping a task in another story, will not be named (docs/specs/full-access.md:37; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/task-plans/CODE.md:141; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:887).

The proposed plan and decision text diff is `git diff <stage base>..HEAD`, so it omits working-tree edits even though the approved review input is the committed diff plus working tree. The plan does not say how those edits become visible to the reviewer or whether close must refuse them (plans/active/FORGE-ACCESS-1-full-access-forge-judges-the-result-not-each-write.md:65; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/task-plans/CODE.md:142).

Removing `quickfix done` leaves a dead-end instruction for a legacy open quickfix window: both the open-window refusal and task-seal preflight still tell the operator to run that removed command. The plan retains `mode abandon` but does not update either instruction (factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:144; factory/scripts/factory_lib.py:5963; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/task-plans/CODE.md:167).

The claimed Windows selector check does not validate the new `test_full_access.py` selector: it parses only `test_gates.py` selectors. A misspelled new selector can pass this check and fail the Windows job (.factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/task-plans/CODE.md:186; factory/tests/test_gates.py:10707; factory/tests/test_gates.py:10719).

The new test file is told to reuse `test_gates`'s `repo` fixture, but that fixture is defined in `test_gates.py`, not a shared fixture module. The plan leaves the fixture import or relocation unstated, so the required tests in `test_full_access.py` have no specified way to collect (factory/tests/test_gates.py:317; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/task-plans/CODE.md:192).

The approved story plan fixes three tasks—REMOVE-LOCK and CLOSE-JUDGES in parallel, then DOCS—while the protected decomposition and saved task plan replace them with one CODE task followed by DOCS. This changes IDs, dependency ordering, PR seams and review size without a corresponding amended, reapproved story plan; the recorder treats graph changes as requiring that authority (plans/active/FORGE-ACCESS-1-full-access-forge-judges-the-result-not-each-write.md:108; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/decomposition.json:6; factory/scripts/record_decomposition_from_json.py:538). The task plan itself concedes the combined work may exceed one session (.factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/task-plans/CODE.md:86).

CODE's acceptance criterion says `strict-role-split` is superseded, but its write scope omits `docs/specs/strict-role-split.md` and the dependent DOCS task owns that status change. CODE cannot deliver its recorded criterion in its own PR (.factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/decomposition.json:17; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/decomposition.json:20; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/decomposition.json:216).

The task has seven acceptance criteria but eight `plan_contracts` statements with different exact wording. No `criteria_map` can have keys equal to both sets as the task-gate contract requires (.factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/decomposition.json:10; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/decomposition.json:159; .factory/stories/FORGE-ACCESS-1/decomposition.json:195).
